elaine (marketing): Hey @devin and @jordan — we need a gated rerun + method checklist for the launch bench claims. Planning to publish latency/cost numbers in the launch blog and want a defensible artifact. Can the runtime team run a controlled sweep and confirm methodology?

devin (runtime): Sure — can you list the exact artifacts you need? eg p50/p95/p99, token counts, model variants, and config? :slightly_smiling_face:

elaine (marketing): Need: p50/p90/p95/p99, cold vs warm starts, quantized (8-bit) vs FP16, throughput at target QPS, warmup protocol, sample payloads, and the raw logs + runseed/commit. Also clear description of traffic profile (seq len distribution).

jordan (eng-runtime): Quick clarifying Qs: which instance types should we use (A100/H100/RTX)? target concurrency and batch size? do you want prefix caching enabled?

elaine (marketing): Prefer H100 if available, fallback A100. Target real-world-ish concurrency: 4–8 concurrent clients, target 200 rps total for the consumer demo slice. Batch size: pick the config that optimizes p95 while staying under 150ms median. Prefix caching: yes for chat flows, but we also need a pure stateless text-gen sweep.

devin (runtime): Got it. We'll run two lanes: (1) chat-warmup with KV cache warmup (simulate ctx re-use), (2) stateless text-gen (no cache). For each lane: FP16, 8-bit quant, and a small quantized+warmup variant. We'll capture per-token breakdowns and latency histograms.

elaine (marketing): Also include a short reproducibility README with the exact command lines, env vars, docker image sha, and commit hash. We may include a short snippet in the blog.

jordan (eng-runtime): Plan/timeline: start run tonight (1732110000) on a reserved slot, full artifact upload by tomorrow EOD. I'll attach commit and config in-thread when scheduled.

priya (product): Friendly ask — can you add a tiny A/B with model variant fallback timings (if we drop from H100->A100) so we can mention graceful degradation? no need to be exhaustive, one representative failure mode.

devin (runtime): Will do. One more thing: do you want synthetic token distribution or our sampled production payloads? Synthetic is faster but less realistic.

elaine (marketing): Use sampled production-ish payloads from the seed cohort we shared last week + one synthetic stress profile with long tails (seq 512). We need a note that synthetic is for stress only.

bench-bot: Run scheduled: job_id=rb-2024-09-18-01, start_ts=1732110000, machines=[h100:2,a100:2], lanes=4. Will post artifacts to /shared/marketing/bench/rb-2024-09-18-01 when done. :robot_face:

jordan (eng-runtime): Uploaded config & commit: git@repo:redwood/inference.git@c3f5a2b. Warmup script attached as gist: https://gist.github.com/rw/warmup-script. We'll ensure logs include seed and random state.

elaine (marketing): Perfect — once artifacts land, I'll validate the p95 claims and ping for any rerun requests. Thanks team :clap:

devin (runtime): Note: if we see >20% variance between runs we'll add a longitudinal repeat and include variance bands.

priya (product): For slide deck — can we get a 1-slide TL;DR of key deltas (quant vs FP16, cold vs warm) so marketing can craft the headline?

jordan (eng-runtime): Yep. We'll prepare a small CSV summary and a screenshot of the heatmap for the p99 tail.

elaine (marketing): Awesome. Closing ask: please call out any caveats (warmup assumptions, caching behavior, and model config) plainly in the README.

bench-bot: Run complete: job_id=rb-2024-09-18-01, finish_ts=1732113476, artifacts_url=/shared/marketing/bench/rb-2024-09-18-01 :white_check_mark:
